Treat these as NOT vulnerabilities unless there is a concrete bypass:
- The Supabase anon key and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL being public (security relies on RLS).
- Test files, fixtures and seed scripts using obvious dummy credentials (e.g. "test", "password123" in *.test.* or seed files).
- Generic hardening advice without an exploitable path (missing headers are Low unless they enable an attack).
- Rate limiting suggestions on endpoints that are already behind authentication and are cheap.
- Theoretical issues in code paths that are unreachable from any entry point.
